note: The island strum on a four-chord loop, built in three sections so no step is a shortcut: the hand moving down and up with every strum played, then the pattern with its misses on one chord, then the pattern round the loop. Each step says where the hand misses the strings and what to do when the pattern breaks.

exercise.title: G, Em, C and D with the island strum
exercise.why: The strumming hand moves down and up on every half beat whether it hits the strings or not, so the misses fall in time by themselves and the pattern never has to be counted.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play, and the arrows in it show the strums: down on each beat and up between the beats.
Strum down, up, down, up through the whole bar, one bar for each chord.
Practice until your hand swings evenly and never stops at a chord change.

tool.pattern: D U D U D U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. The boxes now show a new pattern, the island strum, on G alone: a dot in a box is a miss, where your hand moves but passes the strings without touching them.
Keep your hand moving down and up exactly as before, and let it miss where the dots are.
If the pattern breaks, go back to strumming every down and up for a bar, then leave the misses out again.

tool.pattern: D . D U . U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. The same pattern now goes round G, Em, C and D, one bar for each chord.
Change chord during the last up strum of the bar, so the new chord is ready for the down strum on beat 1.
Practice until the pattern keeps going by itself while you think about the next chord.

tool.pattern: D . D U . U D U
